reference_memory.normal_pattern: The time series exhibits a highly regular, quasi-sinusoidal oscillation with an estimated period of ~182 points, consistent across all candidates. Each cycle consists of a smooth, asymmetric waveform: a relatively gradual descent from peak to trough (~100–110 points), followed by a sharper, steeper ascent back to the next peak (~70–80 points). Peaks are rounded and symmetric in curvature, reaching robust-standardized values between 3.0 and 4.1 (90th-percentile amplitude ~3.9–4.6), while troughs are consistently near −1.0 to −0.8, forming a stable baseline offset. The overall trend is near-zero slope per point (|slope| < 0.001), with candidate 1 showing a slight positive drift and candidate 2 nearly flat—within acceptable variation. Noise is low: roughness metrics (0.030–0.033) indicate minimal high-frequency jitter; curvature (~0.014) confirms gentle, continuous bending without kinks. Boundary truncation is present only in candidate 0 (single-cycle excerpt), which captures a full but incomplete cycle (starts mid-descent, ends mid-ascent), yet still preserves the core morphology. Amplitude varies modestly across cycles (±0.3 in peak height), likely due to natural modulation rather than anomaly. All reliable candidates share identical phase alignment of peaks/troughs relative to cycle start, confirming temporal stability. Acceptable variation includes ±0.2 in median level, ±0.1 in MAD, and minor asymmetry shifts in ascent/descent duration.
